pages: Lightweight Lossless Secret Image Sharing with Digit-wise Decomposition. Abstract: We address the problem of securely sharing a secret image among multiple participants such that any authorized subset can losslessly reconstruct the image while unauthorized subsets learn nothing. The goal is to reduce the size of the generated shadow images without sacrificing lossless recovery.

Objectives. The primary objective is to design a (k, n) threshold secret image sharing scheme whose shadow images are substantially smaller than the secret image, lowering storage and transmission cost, while guaranteeing exact lossless reconstruction of every pixel.

Proposed method. Each pixel value is decomposed digit-wise in a chosen base, and the resulting digits are distributed across shadows using a lightweight polynomial-based sharing step over a small finite field. This digit-wise decomposition is what enables shadow size reduction compared with classic Shamir-based image sharing.

Evaluation. Experiments use standard grayscale test images including Lena, Baboon, and Peppers at 512x512 resolution. Metrics are the shadow size reduction ratio, reconstruction correctness (lossless or not), and the peak signal-to-noise ratio between the secret and reconstructed images.

Results. The scheme achieves lossless reconstruction with infinite PSNR for authorized subsets and reduces shadow size by about 40% relative to a Shamir polynomial baseline, confirming that digit-wise decomposition lowers shadow overhead. Unauthorized subsets recover no useful information.

Limitations and future directions. Current limitations include increased computation for very large images and sensitivity to the chosen decomposition base. Future work includes extension to color images, progressive recovery, and cheating detection among dishonest participants.
